parts.visual:
You have survived 99 lessons of business mechanics, finance, psychology, and strategy. Now, you face the ultimate truth of the CEO.

1. It is lonely: You cannot vent to your employees, and you cannot show panic to your board.
2. You are the Chief Psychology Officer: Your real job is managing the energy and belief of the company.
3. Extreme Ownership: There are no excuses at the top. If the market crashes, it's your fault. If an employee steals, it's your fault. You own it all.
parts.audio: Welcome to the final gauntlet. The CEO mindset requires extreme ownership. There are no excuses at the top. You own the failures, and you give away the credit.

questions.question: A global pandemic shuts down the supply chain. Revenue drops by 40%. The Board asks you why the company missed its targets. What is the CEO's answer?
options: 'It is not my fault, the pandemic was unforeseeable.'
'The responsibility is mine. We lacked a robust contingency plan. Here is how we pivot to digital revenue immediately.'
questions.correct_answer: 'The responsibility is mine. We lacked a robust contingency plan. Here is how we pivot to digital revenue immediately.'
questions.explanation: Extreme Ownership means accepting that while you cannot control the weather, you are absolutely responsible for the strength of the ship.

questions.question: Listen to the greatest leadership paradox. What is the rule?
questions.tts_text: When the company fails, I look in the mirror. When the company succeeds, I look out the window.
options: Take all the blame for failures, and give all the credit for success to your team.
Look out the window to avoid work.
questions.correct_answer: Take all the blame for failures, and give all the credit for success to your team.
questions.explanation: This is the essence of true leadership. It breeds absolute loyalty from your elite performers.

questions.question: Why is the CEO role described as 'Lonely'?
options: Because they have their own office.
Because they must absorb the fears of the entire company, but they have no one internally they can show their own fears to without causing panic.
questions.correct_answer: Because they must absorb the fears of the entire company, but they have no one internally they can show their own fears to without causing panic.
questions.explanation: This is why CEOs heavily rely on external executive coaches and peer networks (like YPO).

questions.question: You have completed the Executive Foundation. What is the ultimate purpose of business?
options: To make as much money as possible and crush competitors.
To solve a meaningful problem in society at scale, generating sustainable profit as a byproduct of the immense value you create.
questions.correct_answer: To solve a meaningful problem in society at scale, generating sustainable profit as a byproduct of the immense value you create.
questions.explanation: Profit is the oxygen of a business, but it is not the purpose of life. Great executives build things that matter.

questions.question: Construct the ultimate mantra of an elite leader:
questions.explanation: You have conquered the Executive Foundation. Welcome to the C-Suite.
